description: Marathon Petroleum is a petroleum and energy refining, processing, and marketing company. Until 2011, it was a fully owned subsidiary of Marathon Oil. MPC operates the largest petroleum refining system in the U.S. as of 2026. The marketing arm includes Marathon-branded retail outlets—gas stations offering Marathon gasoline, plus car washing services and convenience store items. In addition to its refining and fuel businesses, the company makes ingredients for household items such as carpeting and PVC pipes. Through a partnership with MPLX, Marathon Petroleum provides fuel logistics and distribution services.

title: Marathon Petroleum

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Oil and gas refiner Marathon Petroleum brought in $180 billion in revenue, a 27% increase from the previous year. The company made $14.5 billion in profits, an increase of almost 50%.

  • Marathon returned 86.5% to shareholders in 2022, making it the sixth-best-performing stock on the U.S. Fortune 500 for the year.

  • In April 2023, Tesoro Refining and Marketing, which was acquired by Marathon Petroleum in 2018, paid a $27.5 million settlement for violating a court order to reduce pollution at its facility in Martinez, Calif.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Like most energy companies, independent refiner Marathon Petroleum took a big hit from declining oil and gas prices at the start of the pandemic—and saw its fortunes rebound in 2021, climbing from No. 81 to No. 49 on this year’s Global 500. The company also sold gas-station and convenience-store chain Speedway to 7-Eleven for $21 billion in May 2021. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine created new challenges for Marathon in 2022: Prior to the invasion, Marathon was a major purchaser of Russian oil. Owing to sanctions against Russian products, the company has started looking for alternative suppliers; in particular, it has begun turning to Ecuador as a source of crude.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: The country’s largest independent refiner wasn’t spared the ravages of COVID-19. Major disruptions to the transport fuels business saddled Marathon with a $9.8 billion loss in profits in 2020. To consolidate, the company announced it would sell its Speedway retail operations to 7-Eleven for $21 billion. The company also began widespread job cuts shortly after it announced in August the permanent closure of two refineries in New Mexico and California. Adding to its challenges, a devastating winter storm in Texas delayed the company’s 2020 results.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: While much of the energy sector struggled with faltering oil prices, the U.S.’s largest independent refiner eked out gains by processing crude into industrial products.That pushed up revenue 28.5% in 2019 even as net income remained flat. Still, the Ohio-based business had a tumultuous year. It purchased Andeavor, a move that expanded its reach as a refiner, but failed to live up to Marathon's expectations. Activist investors, meanwhile, renewed demands for a management shakeup. They also pushed for a review of the company's pipeline and storage operations, as well as the planned spin-off of its retail Speedway business.
